``` r
library(package = semmcci)
library(package = lavaan)
```

## Data




``` r
summary(object = df)
#>        X                   M                  Y           
#>  Min.   :-3.199558   Min.   :-3.37128   Min.   :-3.61432  
#>  1st Qu.:-0.632676   1st Qu.:-0.70516   1st Qu.:-0.66921  
#>  Median : 0.028235   Median : 0.02825   Median :-0.04833  
#>  Mean   : 0.002688   Mean   :-0.01992   Mean   :-0.01538  
#>  3rd Qu.: 0.657543   3rd Qu.: 0.65240   3rd Qu.: 0.65293  
#>  Max.   : 3.470910   Max.   : 2.93497   Max.   : 3.09950  
#>  NAs    :100         NAs    :100        NAs    :100
```

## Multiple Imputation

Perform the appropriate multiple imputation approach to deal with missing values.
In this example, we impute multivariate missing data under the normal model.


``` r
mi <- mice::mice(
  data = df,
  method = "norm",
  m = 100,
  print = FALSE,
  seed = 42
)
```

## Model Specification


``` r
model <- "
  Y ~ cp * X + b * M
  M ~ a * X
  X ~~ X
  indirect := a * b
  direct := cp
  total := cp + (a * b)
"
```

## Model Fitting


``` r
fit <- lavaan::sem(data = df, model = model)
```

## Monte Carlo Confidence Intervals


``` r
unstd <- MCMI(lav = fit, mi = mi, R = 20000L, alpha = 0.05)
```

## Methods

### print


``` r
print(x = unstd)
#> Monte Carlo Confidence Intervals (Multiple Imputation Estimates)
#>             est     se     R   2.5%  97.5%
#> cp       0.2328 0.0298 20000 0.1743 0.2917
#> b        0.5113 0.0300 20000 0.4530 0.5698
#> a        0.4811 0.0286 20000 0.4254 0.5376
#> X~~X     1.0617 0.0498 20000 0.9633 1.1595
#> Y~~Y     0.5533 0.0273 20000 0.5003 0.6070
#> M~~M     0.7568 0.0363 20000 0.6848 0.8274
#> indirect 0.2460 0.0204 20000 0.2078 0.2873
#> direct   0.2328 0.0298 20000 0.1743 0.2917
#> total    0.4788 0.0283 20000 0.4232 0.5347
```

## Standardized Monte Carlo Confidence Intervals


``` r
fit <- lavaan::sem(data = df, model = model, fixed.x = FALSE)
unstd <- MCMI(lav = fit, mi = mi, R = 20000L, alpha = 0.05)
```


``` r
std <- MCStd(mc = unstd, alpha = 0.05)
```

## Methods

### print


